feedback:
The proposal covers all fourteen named requirements exactly once, but scheduling and meeting acceptance still need decisions before implementation phases can be derived. Revision can resolve these defects using the supplied material. Unperformed runtime experiments do not, by themselves, require a stuck judgment.

The four previous blocking objections are resolved. D-009 defines scoped AX acknowledgment and its qualification conditions. D-009 and D-010 compare persistent Unicode authorization with paste alternatives while preserving delayed-consumer protection. F4 supplies an interaction threshold and a consequence for failure. D-017 assigns translation to GenerationService over a retained transcript. D-006 now owns the backlog definition and thresholds, D-027 accounts for ring storage, and D-030 states the durability scope. Earlier ownership corrections remain intact, including staging-model eligibility, shared-asset protection, diarization checkpoint handoff and deletion fencing. D-025 correctly withholds automatic media restoration where continuing ownership cannot be established.

The recognition-preemption objection identifies a real ambiguity. D-004 permits preemption and restarts stages lacking checkpoints, while D-020 defines recognition windows without defining preserved progress. D-031 separately makes interrupted recognition fail. The review overstates this as guaranteed starvation because the proposal never clearly says when recognition can be preempted. However, restarting a long recognition after each short dictation could repeatedly discard its progress. Define the recognition scheduling unit, ownership of completed-window output and behavior when an execution epoch changes. State whether ordinary preemption preserves progress even when crash recovery deliberately fails the run. Add repeated short dictations during meeting recognition to verification, checking both interactive delay and eventual meeting progress under a stated workload. Checkpointing alone does not supply fairness under an indefinitely saturated higher-priority queue.

F5 defines useful measurements, but speaker-separation quality and identity-editing effort lack acceptance criteria. Notes already have semantic-review criteria elsewhere, so the review's broader claim that meetings have no acceptance basis is excessive. Explain the provisional 600-second window and 570-second step in relation to decoded-window storage, model residency and workspace within the 1.5 GiB estimate. For a two-hour meeting, those parameters produce thirteen windows per stream. Assuming four remote speakers and one local speaker recur throughout, twelve boundaries produce sixty identity-link decisions. Batch confirmation can reduce UI actions, so sixty links must not be reported as sixty unavoidable clicks. Define the effort metric and proposed acceptable burden, along with a diarization-quality criterion and the consequence of failure. These can be explicit provisional criteria without invented measurements. The whole-input reconsideration path already refers to I7 and the resource protocol, so it does have a definition of bounded behavior beyond an unexplained flat graph.

Held delivery needs an explicit transition rule. D-008 defines when a target mismatch holds output, and D-010 dispatches eligible attempts, but neither establishes whether returning focus automatically makes a held attempt eligible. Decide whether an explicit delivery action is required and test a return to the original field after intervening edits. Otherwise implementation determines whether old text can appear unexpectedly. Also specify capture cancellation independently from interruption preservation, or justify the shared preference for each session kind. The existing fixture confirms the selected preference but does not establish that it matches the intended cancellation behavior.

The requested architectural comparison remains incomplete. Evolution explains how the selected ports support new sources and runtime replacement. D-002's alternatives discuss coupling and release coordination without tracing those same changes through an alternative design. Add a short comparison identifying which components, persistent records and interfaces would change under a single-target or in-process design. This does not require detailed implementation phases.

Several review assertions should not become additional blockers. D-024 promises library deletion and expressly acknowledges that external text cannot be undone. It does not promise clipboard clearing, so the claimed contradiction with D-010 is unsupported. Clarify that an unresolved paste can leave deleted text on the clipboard, preserving ownership checks and informed resolution. The resource protocol now specifies sampling and pilot-derived tolerance. Optional LZFSE makes no savings claim and has a reversible publication mechanism. The review supplies no measured document count or evidence establishing its categorical cache-purge claim. Those claims cannot establish defects by assertion. The remaining implementation details should be recorded where they affect observable behavior, especially microphone startup and capture scope, without reopening settled ownership protocols or requiring completed feasibility experiments for design acceptance.
